items.headline: Singtel CEO takes a 17% pay cut to S$6.8 million after a run of network outages
items.summary: Group chief executive Ng Tian Chong's annual pay fell 17% to S$6.8 million after a series of 2026 service disruptions in Singapore and Australia, including a three-day outage in March that affected around 600,000 mobile customers. The board tied the reduction to accountability for network reliability.

items.headline: SIA chief's pay rises to S$9.7 million as the group posts record revenue
items.summary: Singapore Airlines chief executive Goh Choon Phong was paid nearly S$9.7 million for the year to 31 March 2026, up from about S$7 million, as the SIA Group reported record revenue of roughly S$20.5 billion and carried some 42.2 million passengers. The figures were disclosed in the airline's FY2025/26 annual report.

items.headline: All drink containers must carry the 10-cent deposit from 1 July as the return scheme's transition ends
items.summary: Singapore's Beverage Container Return Scheme became fully mandatory on 1 July after a transition period for clearing older stock ended on 30 June. All in-scope plastic bottles and metal cans from 150ml to 3 litres must now carry the deposit mark and a refundable 10-cent deposit, redeemable at designated return points.

items.headline: Teenager and four men arrested over a scheme to fraudulently obtain Singpass and bank accounts
items.summary: The Anti-Scam Command arrested a 17-year-old girl and four men aged 22 to 29 on 1 July for allegedly conspiring with an overseas syndicate to hand over local bank accounts and trick job-seekers into surrendering their Singpass credentials. The accounts were allegedly used to receive scam proceeds.

items.headline: Former bank manager, 65, charged over S$1.72 million missing from a Serangoon Road vault
items.summary: A 65-year-old former branch manager was charged with criminal breach of trust and account falsification for allegedly misappropriating S$1.72 million from a cash vault between December 2021 and August 2022, falsifying balance records on about 200 occasions. Part of the money was allegedly gambled away at Marina Bay Sands.

items.headline: MGNREGA replaced by the new VB-G RAM G rural jobs law from 1 July
items.summary: From 1 July the two-decade-old MGNREGA was replaced by the Viksit Bharat-Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) Act, raising guaranteed work from 100 to 125 days a year, fixing an interim floor wage of Rs 300 a day, and carrying a record Rs 95,692 crore allocation for 2026-27. It also introduces a roughly 60-day pause during peak farming seasons.

items.headline: Gen Dhiraj Seth takes charge as Army Chief in a reshuffle of India's military top brass
items.summary: Gen Dhiraj Seth assumed office as the 31st Chief of the Army Staff, succeeding Gen Upendra Dwivedi and becoming the first officer from the Armoured Corps to lead the Indian Army in nearly three decades. New vice chiefs of the Army and the Air Force also took charge as the top brass was reshuffled around the start of July.

items.headline: Supreme Court declines to disturb the extension of Manipur panchayat polls to October
items.summary: A bench of Justices N. Kotiswar Singh and N.V. Anjaria on 2 July dismissed a plea challenging a Manipur High Court order that pushed the state's panchayat elections to 16 October 2026, citing law-and-order conditions. The petitioners had argued the elected bodies' mandate lapsed nearly four years ago.

items.headline: Sensex jumps 579 points as IT stocks rebound and crude eases
items.summary: The BSE Sensex closed 579 points higher at about 77,502 on 2 July and the Nifty held above 24,175, led by a roughly 4.6% surge in IT stocks as Infosys, TCS and HCL Technologies rebounded after four straight sessions of losses. Softer crude prices and easing Gulf tensions aided sentiment.

items.headline: At least four killed in Mumbai-area monsoon accidents as heavy rain lashes the city
items.summary: A string of monsoon accidents across the Mumbai region killed at least four people around 1-2 July, including a teenager electrocuted in waterlogged Mumbra and an 11-year-old killed when a tree fell on a school bus in Chembur. The deaths renewed demands over civic safety and drainage.

items.headline: Court of Appeal jails two teenagers who had been spared custody for a Fordingbridge rape
items.summary: The Court of Appeal on 2 July ruled the original non-custodial sentences 'unduly lenient' and ordered two 15-year-old boys detained for four years for raping two girls aged 14 and 15. The Lady Chief Justice, Baroness Carr, said the trial judge had wrongly assessed the level of harm.

items.headline: Starmer issues a state apology for decades of forced adoptions of unmarried mothers
items.summary: Prime Minister Keir Starmer told the Commons on 2 July that 'the shame is ours', formally apologising for the state's role in coercing an estimated 185,000 unmarried mothers in England and Wales into giving up their babies between 1949 and 1976. The apology came with a £4 million support package but no compensation.

items.headline: Channel small-boat crossings fall sharply in the first half of 2026
items.summary: Home Office figures show 11,884 migrants crossed the Channel in the first six months of 2026, down from a record 19,982 in the previous half-year, with June the quietest June since 2021. Ministers credited stepped-up French interceptions, though the average number carried per boat rose.

items.headline: Standards commissioner finds Farage broke MPs' rules 17 times over £384,000 in interests
items.summary: The Parliamentary Commissioner for Standards found Reform UK leader Nigel Farage breached the rules on 17 occasions by failing to register financial interests totalling about £384,000 within the 28-day deadline, but concluded the breaches were inadvertent and warranted no sanction.

items.headline: UK business confidence slumps as the IoD's economic sentiment index falls to -61
items.summary: The Institute of Directors said its Economic Confidence Index dropped to -61 in June from -53 in May, its weakest reading this year, as revenue and investment expectations slid. Directors cited rising energy and employment costs.

items.headline: Vatican declares the traditionalist Society of St Pius X in schism and excommunicates its bishops
items.summary: The Vatican on 2 July declared the traditionalist Society of St Pius X (SSPX) in formal schism and excommunicated four newly consecrated bishops and the two who consecrated them, after they defied Pope Leo XIV. Rome also said marriages and confessions performed by SSPX priests are invalid.

items.headline: Germany's Merz coalition agrees a sweeping tax, pension and labour reform package
items.summary: Chancellor Friedrich Merz's CDU/CSU-SPD coalition unveiled a 34-measure 'Programme for Revival and Employment' on 2 July after seven hours of talks, including about €10 billion a year in income-tax relief from 2027, a pension overhaul and tighter sick-leave rules. The package aims to revive the economy and blunt the far right.

items.headline: Update: Russia's largest strike on Kyiv in weeks kills at least 22
items.summary: A massive overnight Russian assault on 2 July killed at least 22 people and wounded more than 85 in Kyiv, as Ukraine's air force reported nearly 500 drones and over 70 missiles launched across the country. A single missile destroyed 64 apartments in a nine-storey residential block.

items.headline: Iran sets a multi-day state funeral for Khamenei as US-Iran talks in Doha report progress
items.summary: Iran announced that the funeral for late Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, killed in the February US-Israeli strikes, will begin in Tehran on 4 July and end with his burial in Mashhad on 9 July. Indirect US-Iran talks in Doha were said to have made 'positive progress', with further discussions expected after the funeral.

items.headline: US judge blocks Trump-backed mail-in ballot restrictions in a win for the NAACP
items.summary: District Judge Emmet Sullivan sided with the NAACP on 1 July, ruling the US Postal Service could not impose proposed mail-in ballot restrictions championed by President Trump because they would likely violate a 2021 settlement requiring expedited handling of ballot mail. It was another court setback for the administration's election agenda.

items.headline: Anthropic is in talks with Samsung to build its own custom AI chip
items.summary: Anthropic is discussing a custom AI chip with Samsung, eyeing the chipmaker's 2nm process, and has hired former OpenAI silicon lead Clive Chan, according to reports. The move would be a first step toward in-house hardware to reduce its reliance on Nvidia, Google and Amazon.

items.headline: OpenAI floats giving the US government a 5% stake to ease Washington scrutiny
items.summary: Sam Altman proposed handing the US government a roughly 5% stake — worth about $42 billion against OpenAI's $852 billion valuation — through an Alaska-fund-style vehicle, and suggested rivals such as Google and Meta do the same. The idea, reported on 2 July, is aimed at easing regulatory pressure.

items.headline: Microsoft launches a $2.5 billion unit to embed 6,000 AI engineers with clients
items.summary: Microsoft unveiled 'Microsoft Frontier', a reported $2.5 billion initiative that will place up to 6,000 engineers inside customer organisations to deploy AI systems, days after Amazon Web Services announced a $1 billion forward-deployed engineering push. The move deepens a race to embed AI teams with enterprises.

items.headline: Privacy-focused Venice AI hits a $1 billion valuation on a $65 million round
items.summary: Venice AI, founded by Erik Voorhees, raised a $65 million Series A led by Dragonfly at a $1 billion valuation — its first outside round — reporting 3.5 million users and more than $70 million in annual recurring revenue. The platform encrypts user prompts on the client side.

items.headline: Video-AI startup TwelveLabs raises $100 million with Amazon backing
items.summary: TwelveLabs raised $100 million, co-led by NEA and NAVER Ventures with participation from Amazon, and named AWS its preferred cloud under a multi-year Trainium commitment. The round takes the video-understanding startup past $200 million in total funding.

items.headline: US adds just 57,000 jobs in June, far below forecasts
items.summary: Non-farm payrolls rose only 57,000 in June against expectations of about 110,000, with unemployment ticking up to 4.2% and the prior two months revised down by a combined 74,000. The weak report cut market-implied odds of a September Federal Reserve rate move.

items.headline: Tesla posts record Q2 deliveries of 480,126 but the stock still falls about 7%
items.summary: Tesla delivered 480,126 vehicles in the second quarter, up 25% year-on-year and its best-ever second quarter, beating estimates of around 406,000. Shares still slid about 7% — the stock's worst day in nearly a year — as the total trailed BYD's EV sales.

items.headline: AOL owner Bending Spoons surges 40% in its $1.68 billion Nasdaq debut
items.summary: Milan-based Bending Spoons, which owns AOL, Evernote and Vimeo, closed its first trading day up about 40% at $40.50 after pricing its IPO at $29, reaching a market value near $25.7 billion. The listing raised $1.68 billion.

items.headline: Gold jumps more than 2% past $4,100 after the weak US jobs report
items.summary: Spot gold climbed about 2.2% to around $4,117 an ounce on 2 July, rebounding from a near seven-month low, as the soft June payrolls print eased fears of a Federal Reserve rate hike. Weaker oil near $67 a barrel added support.

items.headline: Genuine Parts jumps as O'Reilly is reported to bid for its NAPA auto unit
items.summary: Shares of Genuine Parts rose about 13% after Bloomberg reported that O'Reilly Automotive made a cash offer for its NAPA auto-parts business, potentially valued at more than $10 billion. It would be O'Reilly's largest deal since 2008; its own shares fell about 5%.

items.headline: Swiatek reaches the third round as Rybakina and Anisimova also advance
items.summary: Defending champion Iga Swiatek beat former world No. 1 Karolina Pliskova in straight sets to reach the Wimbledon third round, where she meets Alexandra Eala. Second seed Elena Rybakina eased past Caty McNally 6-1, 6-2, and Amanda Anisimova fought back to beat former champion Sofia Kenin.

items.headline: Zverev, de Minaur and Fritz cruise into the Wimbledon third round
items.summary: Second seed Alexander Zverev beat Valentin Royer 6-1, 6-3, 7-6(3) and next faces Marcos Giron, while fifth seed Alex de Minaur dismissed Adrian Mannarino 6-3, 6-2, 6-2. Sixth seed Taylor Fritz also advanced, beating Patrick Kypson in straight sets.

items.headline: England beat South Africa to set up a T20 World Cup final against Australia
items.summary: England won their semi-final against South Africa at The Oval on 2 July, powered by a half-century from captain Nat Sciver-Brunt on her return from a calf injury, to reach the Women's T20 World Cup final. They meet unbeaten Australia at Lord's on Sunday, 5 July.

items.headline: Hamilton eyes a record 10th British GP win on home soil as Ferrari brings upgrades
items.summary: Lewis Hamilton returns to Silverstone for his home Grand Prix already the all-time record-holder with nine British GP wins, with former team-mate Jenson Button backing him to challenge for victory. Ferrari has brought upgrades for the sprint weekend after a difficult Austrian round.

items.headline: Verstappen plays down Red Bull's Silverstone hopes despite an upturn in Austria
items.summary: Max Verstappen tempered expectations for the British Grand Prix, saying Red Bull will keep focusing on its own package after an improved showing in Austria, and admitted Silverstone's high-speed corners felt like a different challenge in the simulator. Silverstone hosts a sprint weekend, its first since 2021.

items.headline: Scientists recover ancient human DNA from cave-art walls for the first time
items.summary: Researchers reported recovering Homo sapiens DNA from a calcite-covered red pigment dot in Portugal's Escoural Cave, part of a study of 11 caves across Spain and Portugal published in Nature Communications. It is the first evidence that cave walls can preserve human genetic material for thousands of years.

items.headline: Webb watches a giant planet survive the death of its star
items.summary: Astronomers used the James Webb Space Telescope to observe the Jupiter-sized planet WD 1856 b transiting the white dwarf it orbits about 80 light-years away, measuring its mass and temperature — around 126°C — and even detecting its atmosphere. The findings, published on 1 July in Nature, offer a first glimpse of a giant planet's fate after its star dies.

items.headline: Rubin Observatory begins its 10-year survey to map the entire southern sky
items.summary: The NSF-DOE Vera C. Rubin Observatory in Chile has begun the Legacy Survey of Space and Time, using the world's largest digital camera to image the southern sky every few nights for a decade. An early test run alone catalogued more than 11,000 previously unknown asteroids.

items.headline: Global oceans record their hottest June ever measured
items.summary: The EU's Copernicus Climate Change Service reported that global sea-surface temperatures averaged about 20.98°C in June, the highest for the month on record, with marine heatwaves affecting a large share of the world's oceans. Scientists warned the trend is pushing marine ecosystems into uncharted territory.

items.headline: A sea anemone protein reveals a 'reversed' antiviral immune system
items.summary: Researchers reported in Nature Ecology and Evolution that a sea anemone protein called CARDIB resembles a key human antiviral sensor but instead suppresses antiviral genes at rest; anemones engineered to lack it accumulated far more virus. The finding complicates assumptions about how animal immune systems evolved.

fun_fact.headline: A blue whale's tongue weighs as much as an elephant
fun_fact.body: A blue whale — the largest animal that has ever lived — has a tongue that can weigh around three tonnes, roughly the weight of an adult elephant. Its heart is about the size of a small piano, weighs some 180 kilograms, and its beat can reportedly be detected from around two miles away. No creature known, living or extinct, has ever grown bigger.

puzzle.title: The Line of Hats
puzzle.body: Four prisoners are given hats drawn from a set of two black and two white; they know the set but cannot see their own hat. Three sit in a line facing a wall (the back man sees the two ahead, the middle man sees one, the front man sees the wall); a fourth is behind the wall and sees no one. Only a certain call of one's own colour is allowed. After a silence, one calls correctly.
puzzle.approach: Work out what each prisoner can deduce from the others' silence, starting with the one who can see the most.
puzzle.answer: The middle man. The back man's silence shows the two hats ahead of him differ; the middle man then knows his own is the opposite of the front man's hat.

word_puzzle.title: Get Well Soon
word_puzzle.body: Turn SICK into WELL in four steps, changing one letter at a time, each rung a real word.
word_puzzle.approach: Change one letter at a time, each step a real word — think of what sits under a window on the way.
